claims.text: The local release groups Bulbapedia raw source rows 126, 127, and 202 under the promotion note Tropical Mega Battle finals participation prize.

The source indices are not contiguous: Exeggutor row 126 and Tropical Wind row 127 sit near the 1999 finals memory, while Lucky Stadium row 202 carries the 2000 Tropical Mega Battle finals participation note. Treat the source-group boundary as source-derived, not official product-boundary proof.

Bulbapedia frames Tropical Mega Battle as an annual Honolulu tournament from 1999 through 2001, with approximately 50 players attending each year and with the event legacy flowing into the later World Championships structure.

Card-specific sources credit Exeggutor to Dr. Ooyama, Tropical Wind to Sumiyoshi Kizuki, and the Tropical Mega Battle Lucky Stadium print to Kouichi Ooyama; the local raw rows themselves do not surface those credits.

This source group is the tournament as social object: bilingual text for international exchange, a finals participation route, a stadium card tied to Hawaii, and artwork that feels closer to event culture than ordinary expansion-set collation.

Agents must preserve the finals participation promotion note, row identity, Exeggutor finish/stock distinction, Tropical Wind print lineage, Lucky Stadium bilingual-vs-regional distinction, and card-specific artist evidence before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Tropical Mega Battle finals participation prize — bilingual tournament memory
narrative.why_it_matters: This is the good stuff: not just three rare old promos, but three different ways a tournament became a keepsake. Exeggutor turns language exchange into the card text itself. Tropical Wind turns hospitality into a visual motif that later World Championships cards keep echoing. Lucky Stadium turns the venue into the card. The agent has to feel that romance while keeping the rails hard: exact promotion note, exact row, exact finish or variant, exact event year where the source supports it.

card_highlights.collector_texture_note: This is not just Exeggutor. It is the card trying to be a handshake: Japanese and English living together on one object, made for a tournament where the point was partly to play across languages. The goofy Ooyama energy matters because it makes the exchange human, but the finish check matters just as much.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Exeggutor as Tropical Mega Battle finals participation prize row 126.
Bulbapedia's Exeggutor page identifies the promotional print as illustrated by Dr. Ooyama and gives the Japanese name ナッシー / Nassy.

Bulbapedia says the card was given to participants of the inaugural Tropical Mega Battle at Hilton Hawaiian Village between August 24 and 27, 1999, and separately reprinted in Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 3.

Bulbapedia distinguishes the Tropical Mega Battle print as regular card stock and the Pokémon Card Trainers Vol. 3 print as glossy card stock, while also noting that both carry a Trainers Vol. 3 bottom-border text. This is a primary identification trap.
Exeggutor matters because it turns international exchange into card grammar: the bilingual text is not decorative, it is the tournament's social purpose printed onto the object.

Agents should preserve row 126, Nassy/Exeggutor identity, bilingual text, non-glossy Tropical Mega Battle route, Dr. Ooyama credit, and the Trainers Vol. 3 glossy lookalike trap before accepting a match.

context.release_name: Tropical Mega Battle finals participation prize

signals: Tropical Mega Battle finals participation prize
card_highlights.assembly_note: Tropical Wind row 127 is a 1999 Tropical Mega Battle participation memory and the beginning of a visual lineage that later Worlds cards keep reworking.
card_highlights.collector_texture_note: Tropical Wind is where the prize stops feeling like a certificate and starts feeling like hospitality. Psyduck in a hammock is funny, soft, almost vacation-brained, and that is exactly why the card became a lasting tournament symbol. It says: you were here, in this weird warm room where the game became international.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Tropical Wind as Tropical Mega Battle finals participation prize row 127.
Bulbapedia's Tropical Wind page credits the 1999 Tropical Mega Battle print to Sumiyoshi Kizuki.

Bulbapedia says Tropical Wind was first released in Japan as a participation prize to all 576 participants in the 1999 Tropical Mega Battle, with a further 10 copies awarded through a Trainers Magazine Vol. 3 lottery.

Bulbapedia describes later Tropical Wind/Tropical Breeze-related reprints across 2001 and Worlds-era commemorative sets, preserving the idea that this card becomes a recurring international tournament motif rather than a one-off checklist oddity.
Tropical Wind matters because its image language is hospitality rather than conquest: Psyduck in a hammock becomes an event-memory device, not just a Trainer effect.

Agents should preserve row 127, Tropical Wind title, 1999 Tropical Mega Battle participation route, Sumiyoshi Kizuki credit, and distinguish this print from Challenge Road, P Promotional, Tropical Breeze, and later Worlds-language/stamped versions.

signals: Tropical Mega Battle finals participation prize
card_highlights.assembly_note: Lucky Stadium row 202 is the bilingual Tropical Mega Battle Stadium print, not one of the eight Japanese World Challenge Summer regional stadiums and not the Neo Destiny/Intro Pack/New York variants.
card_highlights.collector_texture_note: Lucky Stadium is almost too perfect for this catalog: a card about place, printed for a tournament that was itself becoming a place in the memory of the game. Its danger is that there are many Lucky Stadiums; its beauty is that the right one points at Hawaii, exchange, and the weird little infrastructure that made early international Pokémon real.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Lucky Stadium as Tropical Mega Battle finals participation prize row 202 and records the row as a bilingual Stadium/Trainer object.

Bulbapedia says competitors who earned a place at the Tropical Mega Battle Tournament at Hilton Hawaiian Village on August 26-27, 2000 were awarded a bilingual Lucky Stadium print with new artwork by Kouichi Ooyama.

Bulbapedia distinguishes the eight Japanese World Challenge Summer regional Lucky Stadium prints from the Tropical Mega Battle bilingual print and from later Neo Destiny, Intro Pack Neo, and New York City prints.
Bulbapedia's gallery and release notes credit the Tropical Mega Battle Lucky Stadium print to Kouichi Ooyama; other Lucky Stadium variants have different artists.
Lucky Stadium matters because it turns place into card identity: a stadium card awarded at the Hawaii tournament where the venue, language, and artwork all become part of the collectible claim.

Agents should preserve Lucky Stadium row 202, bilingual Tropical Mega Battle print, Kouichi Ooyama credit, and the distinction from regional World Challenge Summer, Neo Destiny, Intro Pack Neo, and New York City variants.
